2.1.1 疾病靶点

从公共数据库DisGeNET, GeneCards, TTD（关键词: “chronic heart failure”,“heart failure”下载CHF靶点(supplementary/Table S3.xlsx)

2.1.2 候选治疗靶点

交集靶点(supplementary/Table S4.xlsx)


# overlapping_target <- read.xlsx("supplementary/Table S4.xlsx")

overlapping.targets <- data.frame(Symbol = intersect(disease.targets$Symbol, ingredients.targets$Symbol)) |>
  left_join(ingredients.targets,by = "Symbol") |>
  distinct(Abbreviation,Symbol)  |>
  group_by(Symbol) |>
  summarise(
    Source = paste(Abbreviation, collapse = ";"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(Abbreviation = Source, Symbol) |>
  arrange(Abbreviation)

cat("治疗靶点总数: ", nrow(overlapping.targets), "\n")

common.targets <- overlapping.targets |>
  dplyr::filter(Abbreviation == "ALRP;AR")
cat("共有靶点数: ",nrow(common.targets),"\n")

alrp.unique.targets <- overlapping.targets |>
  dplyr::filter(Abbreviation == "ALRP")
cat("附子特有靶点数: ",nrow(alrp.unique.targets), "\n")

ar.unique.targets <- overlapping.targets |>
  dplyr::filter(Abbreviation == "AR")
cat("黄芪特有靶点数: ",nrow(ar.unique.targets), "\n")

overlapping.targets.alrp <- ingredients.targets |>
  dplyr::filter(Abbreviation=="ALRP" & Symbol %in% overlapping.targets$Symbol) 

cat("附子成分数: ",
    length(unique(overlapping.targets.alrp$PubChem.CID)),
    "附子靶点数",
    length(unique(overlapping.targets.alrp$Symbol)),
    "\n")


overlapping.targets.ar <- ingredients.targets |>
  dplyr::filter(Abbreviation=="AR" & Symbol %in% overlapping.targets$Symbol) 

cat("黄芪成分数: ",
    length(unique(overlapping.targets.ar$PubChem.CID)),
    "黄芪靶点数",
    length(unique(overlapping.targets.ar$Symbol)),
    "\n")

save(
  overlapping.targets,
  common.targets,
  alrp.unique.targets,
  ar.unique.targets,
  overlapping.targets.alrp,
  overlapping.targets.ar,
  file = "../data/network/all.targets.RData"
)


write.xlsx(overlapping.targets, file = "supplementary/Table S4.xlsx")

text:
4.3 KEGG

4.3.1 全部交集靶点的KEGG富集

# 1. KEGG富集分析
kegg_result <- enrichKEGG(
  gene = gene_entrez$ENTREZID,
  organism = 'hsa',
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  qvalueCutoff = 0.2
)

# 2. 使用 setReadable 将 geneID 列转为 Symbol
kegg_result_symbol <- setReadable(
  kegg_result, 
  OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db, 
  keyType = "ENTREZID"
)


# 3. 提取显著通路的结果表格，取前15或20条
kegg_df <- as.data.frame(kegg_result_symbol)
top_pathways <- head(kegg_df, 20)

save(kegg_df, file = "enrich/kegg.RData")

write.xlsx(
  list(
    `KEGG Top20 pathways` = top_pathways
  ),
  file = "main/Table 1.xlsx"
)

write.xlsx(
  list(
    KEGG = kegg_df
  ),
  file = "supplementary/Table S5.xlsx"
)

# 3. 函数: 计算每条通路中三类靶点的贡献度
split_pathway_contribution <- function(gene_ids, alrp_unique, ar_unique, common) {
  genes_in_pathway <- strsplit(gene_ids, "/")[[1]]
  
  # 计算交集数量
  n_alrp <- sum(genes_in_pathway %in% alrp_unique)
  n_ar <- sum(genes_in_pathway %in% ar_unique)
  n_common <- sum(genes_in_pathway %in% common)
  
  # 计算占比（如果通路总基因数为0则返回0）
  total <- length(genes_in_pathway)
  if(total == 0) return(c(0,0,0))
  
  return(c(n_alrp/total, n_ar/total, n_common/total))
}

# 应用拆分函数
contribution_matrix <- t(sapply(top_pathways$geneID, function(x) {
  split_pathway_contribution(x, alrp.unique.targets$Symbol, ar.unique.targets$Symbol, common.targets$Symbol)
}))

colnames(contribution_matrix) <- c("ALRP_Ratio", "AR_Ratio", "Common_Ratio")

# 4. 根据最大贡献贴上"主导类型"标签
final_plot_data <- cbind(top_pathways, contribution_matrix) |>
  mutate(
    Dominant = case_when(
      ALRP_Ratio >= AR_Ratio & ALRP_Ratio >= Common_Ratio ~ "ALRP-driven",
      AR_Ratio >= ALRP_Ratio & AR_Ratio >= Common_Ratio ~ "AR-driven",
      TRUE ~ "Synergistic"
    ),
    # 调整一下顺序，让图例好看
    Dominant = factor(Dominant, levels = c("ALRP-driven", "AR-driven", "Synergistic"))
  )

# 5. 绘制终极气泡图（按主导类型着色）
p <- ggplot(final_plot_data, aes(x = Count, y = reorder(Description, Count))) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Count, color = Dominant), alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "ALRP-driven" = "#E41A1C",    # 附子红
      "AR-driven" = "#377EB8",      # 黄芪蓝
      " Synergistic" = "#4DAF4A")) + # 协同绿
  labs(title = "KEGG Pathway Enrichment (Contributions Classified)",
       x = "Gene Count", y = "Pathways", color = "Contribution Type") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

p

title: The Synergistic Mechanisms of Astragali Radix–Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure: An Integrated Study of Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Molecular Docking
section: 2.1 Chemical Component Dataset Construction and Target Screening
text:
2.1 Chemical Component Dataset Construction and Target Screening
Based on previously validated UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS profiling data of Qifu decoction reported in published studies, a total of 82 chemical constituents of the AR-ALRP medicinal plant pair were systematically identified, including 47 in vitro components extracted from raw AR and ALRP plant materials and 35 in vivo blood-absorbed prototype components detected in drug-containing rat serum after oral administration. All identified components were standardized via the PubChem database to obtain unified molecular identifiers, including PubChem CID, InChIKey, molecular formula, molecular weight, and SMILES structural information. As the present study focused on bioinformatics mechanism exploration rather than phytochemical identification, all chemical component data were sourced from authoritative published experiments. A high-quality, bioavailability-based standardized chemical dataset of the AR-ALRP medicinal plant pair was successfully established, with detailed structural information of all constituents summarized in Table 1 (G). The overall process of chemical component screening and target screening is visualized in ?@fig-2a.
Through integration and de-duplication of multiple public databases, 327 AR-derived target genes and 289 ALRP-derived target genes were retrieved. A total of 1248 validated CHF-related disease targets were screened from DisGeNET, GeneCards, and TTD databases. Venn analysis identified 261 non-redundant AR-ALRP-CHF intersecting targets, consisting of 97 AR-specific targets, 83 ALRP-specific targets, and 81 co-expressed targets. The Venn diagram of target intersection analysis is presented in ?@fig-2b, intuitively showing the overlapping and unique target distributions among AR, ALRP and CHF. A component-target interaction network was constructed to visualize the binding relationship between plant-derived bioactive components and CHF therapeutic targets (?@fig-2c), reflecting the multi-component and multi-target therapeutic characteristics of the AR-ALRP medicinal plant pair. Table 1 (A) summarizes the representative bioactive components of AR and ALRP with verified in vivo absorption, as well as their basic standardized structural information annotated via PubChem.

title: The Synergistic Mechanisms of Astragali Radix–Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure: An Integrated Study of Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Molecular Docking
section: 2.2 PPI Network Analysis and Core Hub Gene Screening
text:
2.2 PPI Network Analysis and Core Hub Gene Screening
The 261 intersecting targets were imported into the STRING database to construct a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network with a confidence threshold of 0.7, yielding 258 valid protein nodes and 3876 interaction edges after removing isolated invalid nodes. The visualized PPI network is shown in ?@fig-3a. Three core topological parameters (MCC, Degree, Betweenness) of each node were calculated via the cytoHubba plug-in, and rank aggregation analysis was performed to screen out the top 25 core hub genes closely associated with CHF treatment. The ranking distribution of these hub genes is displayed in ?@fig-3b. Among them, AKT1, STAT3, IL6, HDAC1, and HSP90AB1 showed the highest topological importance, serving as the core regulatory nodes of AR-ALRP against CHF. Table 1 (B) lists the top 10 core hub genes with detailed topological parameters and functional annotations, and the complete topological information of all 25 hub genes is provided in Table 1 (H). MCODE module analysis further identified 5 key functional modules, which were mainly involved in the regulation of myocardial inflammation, cell survival, and fibrosis progression.

section: 2.3 Subcellular and Tissue Localization Characteristics of Core Targets
text:
2.3 Subcellular and Tissue Localization Characteristics of Core Targets
Subcellular localization prediction based on DeepLoc 2.0 and WoLF PSORT platforms showed that the core hub proteins were mainly distributed in the nucleus, cytoplasm, and cell membrane. The detailed subcellular localization distribution of all hub genes is illustrated in ?@fig-4c and Table 1 (I). Co-regulated hub genes were predominantly localized in the nucleus and cytoplasm, participating in gene transcription and intracellular signal transduction. Targets specifically regulated by AR were enriched in cytoplasm and mitochondria, while ALRP-specific targets were mainly distributed in cell membrane and nucleus, showing distinct spatial distribution differences. The medicinal source distribution and topological parameter comparison of AR-specific, ALRP-specific and co-expressed targets are displayed in ?@fig-4a and ?@fig-4b. Tissue expression analysis based on BioGPS and HPA databases verified that all core hub genes were highly expressed in human cardiac tissue, confirming the cardiac targeting property of AR-ALRP bioactive components. The comprehensive tissue expression profile of hub genes in 84 human organs is shown in Figure 1 (R), and the immunohistochemical staining results of core genes in cardiac tissues are presented in Figure 1 (S). AR-derived targets were widely distributed in immune and metabolic tissues, while ALRP-derived targets exhibited higher cardiac tissue specificity.

title: The Synergistic Mechanisms of Astragali Radix–Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure: An Integrated Study of Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Molecular Docking
section: 2.4 Functional Enrichment Analysis of Core Targets
text:
2.4 Functional Enrichment Analysis of Core Targets
GO and KEGG functional enrichment analyses were performed on 261 intersecting targets to explore the potential biological functions and signaling pathways of AR-ALRP in CHF treatment. GO enrichment results indicated that the target genes were mainly enriched in biological processes including inflammatory response regulation, myocardial cell apoptosis, and cardiac muscle contraction; molecular functions focused on cytokine activity and protein kinase binding; cellular components were consistent with subcellular localization results. The top GO functional enrichment terms are visualized in ?@fig-6a, and all significant GO entries are listed in Table 1 (J) and Figure 1 (Y). KEGG pathway analysis screened 15 significantly enriched signaling pathways, including PI3K-AKT, NF-κB inflammatory, and MAPK pathways, which are classic pathological pathways mediating CHF progression. The top enriched KEGG pathways are shown in ?@fig-6b, with full detailed information provided in Table 1 (K) and Figure 1 (W). Target source decomposition confirmed that key pathways were co-regulated by AR and ALRP-derived targets, and the pathway target source distribution is displayed in ?@fig-6c. Table 1 (C) and Table 1 (D) display the top 10 significantly enriched GO terms and KEGG pathways, respectively.

section: 2.5 Immune Infiltration Characteristics of CHF Samples
text:
2.5 Immune Infiltration Characteristics of CHF Samples
Based on the GSE57338 clinical dataset, the CIBERSORT algorithm was used to analyze the infiltration level of 22 immune cell subtypes in CHF and normal myocardial tissues. The differential infiltration profiles of immune cells between the two groups are intuitively shown in ?@fig-7a. The results showed significant differences in the proportions of M1/M2 macrophages, regulatory T cells, and neutrophils between the two groups. Correlation analysis revealed that core hub genes were significantly correlated with differential immune cells, and the correlation heatmap of hub genes and key immune cell subtypes is presented in ?@fig-7b. The consistency verification of immune infiltration results calculated by CIBERSORT and ssGSEA algorithms is displayed in Figure 1 (T). Plant-specific targets of AR and ALRP showed distinct correlation trends with pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory immune cells, enabling effective regulation of the cardiac immune microenvironment. Table 1 (E) lists the differential infiltration levels of key immune cell subtypes in CHF and normal tissues.

title: The Synergistic Mechanisms of Astragali Radix–Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure: An Integrated Study of Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Molecular Docking
section: 2.6 Clinical Expression Validation of Core Hub Genes
text:
2.6 Clinical Expression Validation of Core Hub Genes
Differential expression analysis of the GSE57338 dataset demonstrated that 22 of the 25 core hub genes were significantly differentially expressed in CHF tissues. The overall differential expression pattern of hub genes is shown in the volcano plot (?@fig-8b), and the complete differential expression data are summarized in Table 1 (L) and Figure 1 (U). Representative core genes AKT1, STAT3, and IL6 were markedly upregulated, while HDAC1 and HSP90AB1 were significantly downregulated in CHF samples. The expression box plots of representative core genes are displayed in ?@fig-8a, and the box plots of all hub genes are supplemented in Figure 1 (V). ROC curve analysis verified that the top five core hub genes possessed excellent diagnostic efficacy for CHF (AUC > 0.75), and the ROC curves of core diagnostic genes are shown in ?@fig-8c, confirming the clinical reliability of the screened core therapeutic targets of AR-ALRP.

title: The Synergistic Mechanisms of Astragali Radix–Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure: An Integrated Study of Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Molecular Docking
text:
2.7 Upstream Regulatory Network Analysis
A TF-miRNA-mRNA three-layer regulatory network was constructed using TRRUST and miRNet databases to explore the upstream epigenetic regulatory mechanism of core hub genes. The visualized multi-layer regulatory network is shown in ?@fig-9a. A total of 18 key transcription factors and 32 functional miRNAs were identified to target and regulate core CHF therapeutic genes. The detailed regulatory relationships between transcription factors/miRNAs and core genes are listed in Table 1 (M) and Table 1 (N). Key upstream regulators including TP53, RELA, hsa-miR-21-5p, and hsa-miR-155-5p were verified to mediate the transcription and post-transcriptional modification of core hub genes, revealing the multi-level regulatory mechanism of AR-ALRP in CHF intervention.

title: The Synergistic Mechanisms of Astragali Radix–Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure: An Integrated Study of Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Molecular Docking
text:
2.8 Molecular Docking Verification
Molecular docking was performed between representative bioactive components of AR-ALRP and core target proteins via CB-Dock2. All compound-target pairs exhibited stable binding affinity with Vina Score < -5.0 kcal/mol. Typical ALRP component benzoylaconine and AR component calycosin could form stable hydrogen bond interactions with key amino acid residues of core target proteins, providing direct molecular structural evidence for the therapeutic activity of AR-ALRP medicinal plant pair against CHF. The 3D docking conformation of representative compound-target pairs is displayed in ?@fig-9b, and the full docking conformation diagrams of all groups are shown in Figure 1 (X). Table 1 (F) summarizes the detailed molecular docking affinity results of key compound-target pairs, and the complete docking data are supplemented in Table 1 (O).

title: The Synergistic Mechanisms of Astragali Radix–Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure: An Integrated Study of Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Molecular Docking
section: 4.1 Construction of Chemical Component Dataset for AR-ALRP Medicinal Plant Pair
text:
4.1 Construction of Chemical Component Dataset for AR-ALRP Medicinal Plant Pair
To obtain candidate bioactive compounds with reliable in vivo systemic exposure basis for subsequent target prediction, the chemical components of the Astragali Radix–Aconiti Radix Lateralis Preparata medicinal plant pair were extracted from validated UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS profiling data of Qifu decoction, which characterized constituents in both herbal raw extracts and rat serum samples after intragastric administration . All identified components were categorized into in vitro components from raw medicinal plant extracts and in vivo blood-absorbed prototype components from drug-containing serum. In vivo circulating components were defined as primary bioactive candidates due to actual systemic exposure, while in vitro plant components were reserved as supplementary candidates to enrich the chemical dataset.
All candidate compounds were standardized and annotated via the PubChem database (https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/, accessed on 2026-02-15) . Standard molecular information including PubChem CID, InChIKey, molecular formula, molecular weight, canonical SMILES, and connectivity SMILES was retrieved, and corresponding SDF structural files were downloaded. All standardized chemical information was summarized to construct a complete and unified chemical component library of the AR-ALRP medicinal plant pair, providing accurate structural data for subsequent target prediction and bioinformatics analysis.

title: The Synergistic Mechanisms of Astragali Radix–Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure: An Integrated Study of Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Molecular Docking
section: 4.2 Multi-Source Target Prediction and Data Quality Control
text:
4.2 Multi-Source Target Prediction and Data Quality Control
Multiple public medicinal bioinformatics databases were integrated to predict the target genes of AR and ALRP bioactive components, including PubChem, Super-PRED, STITCH 5.0, SwissTargetPrediction, PharmMapper, and SEA . All databases were uniformly accessed on 2026-02-15. To ensure data reliability, targets appearing in no less than two independent databases were retained for AR, while all high-confidence predicted and verified targets were retained for ALRP to avoid missing effective functional targets of toxic medicinal plants. All target names were unified to standard HGNC gene symbols for subsequent analysis.

title: The Synergistic Mechanisms of Astragali Radix–Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure: An Integrated Study of Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Molecular Docking
section: 4.3 Acquisition of Chronic Heart Failure Disease Targets
text:
4.3 Acquisition of Chronic Heart Failure Disease Targets
CHF-related disease targets were retrieved from DisGeNET, GeneCards, and TTD databases with strict screening thresholds to ensure data accuracy. The access time of all databases was 2026-02-18. After removing duplicate and low-confidence targets, a total of 1248 valid CHF disease targets were obtained. The R VennDiagram package was used to screen intersecting targets between plant component targets and CHF disease targets, and classify them into plant-specific and co-shared targets.

title: The Synergistic Mechanisms of Astragali Radix–Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure: An Integrated Study of Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Molecular Docking
section: 4.4 PPI Network Construction and Hub Gene Screening
text:
4.4 PPI Network Construction and Hub Gene Screening
The intersecting targets were imported into the STRING 11.5 database to construct a human PPI network with an interaction confidence greater than 0.700. Isolated nodes without interaction relationships were removed, and Cytoscape 3.9.1 was used for network visualization. The cytoHubba plug-in was adopted to calculate MCC, Degree, and Betweenness topological parameters of each node, and the top 25 core hub genes were screened by rank aggregation method. The MCODE plug-in was used for functional module clustering of the PPI network with a score threshold greater than 2.5.

title: The Synergistic Mechanisms of Astragali Radix–Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure: An Integrated Study of Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Molecular Docking
text:
4.5 Multi-Dimensional Bioinformatics Analysis
DeepLoc 2.0 and WoLF PSORT were used to predict the subcellular localization of core hub proteins. DAVID, BioGPS, and HPA databases were combined to analyze the tissue expression distribution characteristics of core targets in human organs. The R clusterProfiler package was used to perform GO and KEGG enrichment analysis of intersecting targets with p < 0.05 and FDR < 0.01 as screening criteria. The GSE57338 dataset from the GEO database was used for immune infiltration analysis via the CIBERSORT algorithm and clinical differential expression verification of hub genes. The pROC package was used for ROC curve analysis to evaluate the diagnostic efficacy of core genes.

title: The Synergistic Mechanisms of Astragali Radix–Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure: An Integrated Study of Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Molecular Docking
text:
4.6 Upstream Regulatory Network Construction
The TRRUST database was used to predict transcription factors regulating core hub genes, and the miRNet database was applied to screen targeted miRNAs of core genes. A TF-miRNA-mRNA three-layer upstream regulatory network was constructed and visualized by Cytoscape software to explore the epigenetic regulatory mechanism of AR-ALRP components.

title: The Synergistic Mechanisms of Astragali Radix–Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure: An Integrated Study of Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Molecular Docking
text:
4.7 Molecular Docking Analysis
The 3D structural files of representative AR-ALRP bioactive components were downloaded from PubChem, and the crystal structures of core target proteins were obtained from the PDB database. Blind molecular docking was performed via CB-Dock2 with Vina Score < −5.0 kcal/mol as the effective binding threshold. PyMOL and Discovery Studio software were used to visualize docking conformations and analyze molecular interaction forces.

title: The Synergistic Mechanisms of Astragali Radix–Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure: An Integrated Study of Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Molecular Docking
text:
Abstract
Background: Chronic heart failure (CHF) lacks comprehensive clinical interventions. Diverse Asian medicinal plants exert multi-target therapeutic effects on CHF, while the molecular mechanism of the medicinal plant pair Astragali Radix–Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata (AR-ALRP) remains unclear. Methods: This study constructed a standardized AR-ALRP chemical dataset via UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS data and PubChem annotation. Multi-source bioinformatics analysis, clinical dataset validation, and molecular docking were performed to screen core therapeutic targets and pathways. Results: In total, 82 plant-derived components and 261 AR-ALRP-CHF intersecting targets were identified, with 25 core hub genes such as AKT1 and IL6. Key genes were clinically dysregulated in CHF, and major plant components stably bound core targets to regulate inflammation and myocardial repair pathways. Conclusions: This study elucidates the multi-component and multi-target mechanism of AR-ALRP against CHF, providing novel insights for cardiovascular application of medicinal plant resources.
Keywords: medicinal plant pair; Astragali Radix; Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata; chronic heart failure; bioinformatics analysis; molecular docking; therapeutic mechanism
